name: Identity / agentic-identity layer
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: The identity-platform segment is dominated by VERTICAL PRODUCT vendors (KYC + IDV + ongoing risk decisioning) on top of proprietary identity graphs and consortium data, NOT generic feature backends. Generic real-time stacks named inside these vendors today: Redis (counters + Lua + Bloom/CMS/Top-K via Redis Stack) is the rolled-own default for per-applicant / per-device / per-IP velocity (Redis published 'Digital Identity Validation with Redis: Real-Time Device Fingerprinting' as a direct architectural analog); the Apr 2024 RSALv2/SSPLv1 relicense + the Linux-Foundation BSD-3 Valkey fork (default 'redis-server' in Ubuntu 26.04) split this default into a license-clean and a relicensed branch. Aerospike at very high cardinality (used inside several of the identity-fraud vendors). DragonflyDB for low-spend in-memory counter workloads. Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers building this in SQL on top of Kafka (RisingWave's 'Real-Time Features for Account Takeover Detection' blog is the public reference). Online feature stores (Tecton-after-Databricks-acq, Hopsworks, Chalk, Fennel-after-Databricks-acq, Feast) are an awkward fit at the inline-decision path - they target ML serving from a central warehouse, not <50ms decision-time velocity features inside an auth gate or onboarding API. Custom in-Rust / in-Go services on top of RocksDB / Sled / FoundationDB are the documented Castle / Fingerprint / Incognia / Socure-Sigma-Device shape inside the vendor. The realistic competition for beava in this segment is Redis-on-Lua (post-relicense) + in-house Rust/Go - NOT the identity vendors themselves, which are buyers and embedders, not competitors.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The named domain incumbents are uniformly proprietary identity-platform vendors selling a productised end-to-end stack (KYC + IDV + device intelligence + ATO + ongoing risk + workflow orchestration). Active 2025-2026 players (funding and product signals): Persona ($200M Series D at $2B valuation May 2025, co-led Founders Fund + Ribbit Capital; explicitly positioned as 'the verified identity layer for an agentic AI world'; signal customers OpenAI, LinkedIn, Roblox, Heritage Bank, Lime; ranked #1 across all use cases in 2024 Gartner Critical Capabilities for IDV and highest Ability-to-Execute in inaugural Gartner Magic Quadrant for IDV; offers Workflows orchestration + Events + Webhooks + a 'Workforce IDV' refresh Jun 2025 detecting 50+ AI-generated spoofing classes; OpenAI screens millions of users / month across 225 countries via Persona). Socure (RiskOS launched Feb 2025 - 'first risk decisioning engine built on the industry's most comprehensive identity graph', powered by Effectiv acquisition; 4B+ known outcomes / 2,800 customers / 40 industries / 314M recurring identities / 96.4% identity recurrence rate; SocureGov RiskOS launched Feb 2026 - FedRAMP Moderate authorisation Mar 2025, used by 130+ public-sector orgs; RiskOS AI Agents and Assistants suite Oct 2025; Local Graph in RiskOS Dec 2025; Sigma Identity Fraud V5, Sigma Synthetic Fraud, Sigma Device; payment screening Feb/Mar 2026; Plaid + Unit21 partnerships). ID.me ($340M Series E + credit facility at $2B+ valuation Sep 2025, total funding $1.1B, led by Ribbit Capital with Ares Credit Funds, Moonshots Capital, Positive Sum; 152M users = ~60% of US adults, 20 federal agencies, 45 states, 600+ brands; explicitly raising to combat AI-driven fraud at the documented $521B annual US cost). Incode ($150-300M raise discussed at up to $3B valuation Nov 2025; $170M ARR; processed 4.1B identity checks in 2024; serves 8 of America's top 10 banks, 8 of NA's top 9 telcos, 4 of LatAm's top 5 banks; acquired AuthenticID Aug 2025 explicitly to fight agentic AI / deepfake / synthetic identity attacks; subcontractor on $37.4M Login.gov Next Generation Identity Proofing contract Dec 2025). Sumsub ($1B+ checks verified, joined WEF Unicorn community 2025; Identity Fraud Report 2025-2026 documents shift to multi-step attacks 10% to 28% YoY and AI-assisted forgery 0% to 2%; integrated Fingerprint Pro Device Intelligence Jun 2025 - 100+ device signals, Smart Signals, 'stop fraud BEFORE it starts based on device signals'; finding: 76% of fraud happens post-KYC, mandating continuous monitoring). Onfido (acquired by Entrust Apr 2024 at $650M; $130M+ ARR pre-acq, 1,200+ customers; integrated into Entrust IAM and digital-signing portfolio as the 'identity-centric security' platform). Trulioo (GlobalGateway pricing $99/mo entry, marketplace of 5B+ people / 330M+ businesses globally). Veriff / Jumio / SEON / Sardine / ComplyAdvantage / Alloy / Unit21 round out the orchestration-and-fraud layer. The 2026 'agentic-identity' wave specifically: World (Sam Altman) shipped AgentKit Apr 2026 with Okta / Vercel / Browserbase / Exa as partners; Prove launched the Prove Identity Platform Apr 2026 as 'the trust layer for an agentic world' on OpenAI / Anthropic / Salesforce frameworks; Google Cloud Fraud Defense launched 2026 with agent-specific bot-vs-human-vs-agent capabilities; OpenAI + Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol Sep 2025. None of these vendors competes for beava's actual sale: they are potential EMBEDDERS of (or upstream of, or downstream of) a feature backend like beava.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed. PRODUCT-level incumbents (Persona, Socure, ID.me, Incode, Sumsub, Onfido/Entrust, Trulioo, Veriff, Jumio, SEON, Sardine, Alloy, Unit21, Prove, World AgentKit) are uniformly proprietary commercial SaaS - NO Apache-2.0 competitors in the IDV / agentic-identity vertical at any meaningful scale. The BACKEND-level incumbent (Redis) is the locked buyer filter: Redis 7.4+ is RSALv2/SSPLv1 dual-licensed (non-OSI, classified non-OSS by Fedora / Debian / AWS / Google / Ubuntu); Valkey BSD-3 (Linux Foundation, AWS/Google/Oracle-backed, default 'redis-server' in Ubuntu 26.04) is the procurement-clean drop-in. Redis 8 (May 2025) added an AGPLv3 option in a tri-license but the cloud-default migration continues toward Valkey. Beava's Apache-2.0 + no-open-core posture is a real wedge specifically against (a) a Persona / Socure / Sumsub / Castle / Fingerprint internal platform team that is rolling its own velocity feature backend on Redis and got caught flat-footed by the Apr 2024 relicense, and (b) any of these vendors that wants to embed a feature backend WITHOUT a competitor's managed-cloud dependency. License is now a hard procurement filter inside these vendors' platform teams, not a preference.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium. Lower than account-abuse / bot-defence (V3, where Cloudflare BM is a direct bundle) and lower than payment-fraud (V1, where Stripe Radar dominates SMB) - because identity verification at the KYC layer is a CONSORTIUM-DATA business that hyperscalers do not own and cannot replicate. AWS does not run a KYC / IDV graph; Azure does not; GCP launched Google Cloud Fraud Defense in 2026 with agent-specific bot/human/agent classification but is positioning it as complementary to (not a replacement for) the IDV vendors. The hyperscalers DO bundle adjacent capabilities that compress the velocity-features-only opportunity beava is sized for: AWS Cognito + Cognito advanced security features (risk-based authentication, compromised credentials check, anomalous-login detection), Azure AD B2C / Entra ID Protection (impossible-travel, sign-in risk, P2-tier ML on trillions of signals), Google Identity Platform + reCAPTCHA Enterprise. These are 'good enough' velocity-and-risk-signal bundles inside the hyperscaler subscription. The threat is sharpest in the impossible-travel sub-domain (use case 19) where Microsoft Entra ID Protection P2 ships impossible-travel as a built-in checkbox and is the obvious-default for any Azure-fronted enterprise. Beava can still win as (a) the EMBEDDED feature backend underneath an IDV vendor that does NOT want to rent from a hyperscaler, (b) inside in-house identity teams at fintechs / marketplaces with multi-cloud or on-prem constraints, and (c) the explicit not-in-Entra / not-in-Cognito buyers (consumer platforms, gaming, dating, crypto, non-financial SaaS).
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Producers in this segment are auth services, KYC orchestrators, and device-intel SDK ingestion pipelines - NOT Kafka/Spark warehouses. Expected upstreams: IDP auth services (Auth0, Okta, Microsoft Entra, WorkOS, Stytch, Descope, Clerk, Frontegg, FusionAuth, SuperTokens, Curity) emitting login_attempt / login_success / signup / password_reset / otp / mfa_step_up; KYC orchestration platforms (Alloy, Unit21, Persona Workflows, Socure RiskOS - itself an orchestrator) emitting identity-verification-event webhooks; device-intel SDKs (Castle, Fingerprint, Incognia, Sardine, Sumsub Device Intelligence, Socure Sigma Device) pushing identify / device-fp / behaviour events through a CDN-fronted ingestion API; WAF / reverse proxy (Cloudflare Worker, Fastly Compute, Envoy, Nginx) emitting auth-related access events; mobile SDKs pushing GPS + device events directly. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the IDP webhook + KYC-orchestrator-webhook + Workers/Compute producer paths; framed-TCP :8081 fits the high-throughput auth-service-sidecar + device-intel-ingestion-shim paths. The Kafka-first feature-store assumption (Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks) is REVERSED here - identity-platform internal teams (Persona, Socure, Castle, Fingerprint, Incognia, Sumsub, Sardine) explicitly do NOT want a broker hop on the <50ms inline-decision path; the slow path (analytics, ML training, consortium-graph build) still goes to Kafka/Kinesis but the hot velocity-feature path is broker-free, which is beava's exact pitch. Friction is on the CLIENT side: IDV vendor teams live in Go / Rust / Java / Node, not Python; beava ships a Python SDK + language-agnostic wire (TCP+msgpack, HTTP+JSON) but does not yet ship Go / Rust / Java / Node client SDKs which is the gap to remove for serious in-vendor adoption. The IP-geolocation enrichment step (MaxMind GeoIP2, IPinfo, ipregistry) is upstream of beava and a documented producer responsibility - the conventional split that Castle / Fingerprint / WorkOS Radar all use.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with strong separation. The dominant pattern across every named identity vendor is a deterministic rules layer (configurable per-customer policies in Socure RiskOS no-code rule builder, Persona Workflows, Castle policies, Sardine policy engine, Alloy / Unit21 case-management rules) PLUS one or more ML risk scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / GNN for device-graph clustering; Socure publishes 4B-outcome consortium-trained models; Persona ships 50+ AI-spoof-class detectors; Sardine publishes a 4,800-feature feature store feeding both rules and ML). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from both - this is the natural seam and the SAME seam beava occupies in account-abuse (V3) and impossible-travel (use case 19). Sardine's published 'feature store feeds rules engine + ML engine' shape is the explicit public reference architecture beava would slot into.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Six concrete reasons a buyer in this segment - SPECIFICALLY an identity-platform internal platform team (Persona, Socure, Castle, Fingerprint, Incognia, Sumsub, Sardine, Sift Device, IPQS, ID.me, an in-house IDP at a fintech / marketplace) - would pick beava over Redis-on-Lua or a custom Rust-on-RocksDB build today: (1) The geo_velocity / geo_distance / geo_spread / distance_from_home primitives (python/beava/_agg.py + crates/beava-core/src/agg_geo.rs) are FIRST-CLASS and ship in the box - this is the cleanest competitive wedge across the entire identity domain, since Redis exposes GEOADD/GEODIST but velocity-between-consecutive-events is hand-rolled Lua, Flink/Materialize need user-defined functions, and Tecton/Feast push it to user-written PySpark. Impossible-travel (use case 19) is the flagship demo opportunity and a 1-day build on existing primitives. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (counters, n_unique HLL, velocity, rate, distribution, distance, entropy, last-N) cover per-applicant / per-device / per-IP / per-(visitor_id x asset_id) features that Fingerprint Velocity Signals, Sumsub Device Intelligence, Castle behavioural velocity, Sardine 4,800-feature feature store, and Socure Sigma Device all productise - external validation that the SHAPE is right. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the <50ms inline auth / KYC decision budget; Persona / Socure / Castle / Fingerprint all measure themselves on inline response time and a broker-free feature backend is structurally lower-latency than a Kafka-fronted feature store. (4) Apache-2.0 with NO open-core, NO managed-cloud requirement - attractive to identity-platform vendors that are themselves commercial vendors and refuse to depend on a competitor's managed cloud OR on Redis Source-Available. This wedge is sharpest post-Apr-2024 Redis relicense. (5) Push-on-event single-binary model maps to the per-region SDK-ingestion topology Persona / Sumsub / Fingerprint / Incognia / Socure already operate, without a Kafka hop on the hot path; the slow path (consortium graph, analytics, ML training) stays on Kafka where it belongs. (6) Composite-key story ((account_id_hash, device_fp), (visitor_id, asset_id_hash), (visitor_id, tenant_id), (ip x route)) is first-class via @bv.table - the canonical mule / multi-accounting / synthetic-identity signal that on Redis is hand-rolled with key-naming conventions. NOTE: beava CANNOT and SHOULD NOT try to replicate the identity-graph data moats - Persona's network, Socure's 4B-outcome consortium, Incognia's 4.1B identity checks, Sumsub's 1B+ check history, Fingerprint's 2.3B-ID dataset are years-of-data assets beava has no path to. Beava's wedge is to be the velocity-feature compute substrate UNDERNEATH these vendors' decision engines, with their consortium-label feeds joined at decision time.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking adoption in this segment today (derived from use cases 2, 19, 20): (1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 in v0 - disqualifying for any external-facing deployment by a SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / FedRAMP / PSD3 / DORA-regulated buyer; effectively limits beava today to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. Persona / Socure / ID.me / Incode are all SOC 2 + FedRAMP-Moderate-grade buyers whose internal platform teams cannot deploy a feature backend without authN/Z and audit logging. (2) No in-process sharding and no replication - a Fingerprint-scale 10^8 to 10^9 visitor_id keyspace cannot fit on one box, and Socure's 314M recurring identities + Incognia's 4.1B checks similarly require horizontal sharding. Redis Cluster / Aerospike / FoundationDB ship this; beava does not. This is the single largest architectural blocker for adoption inside a Fingerprint-scale vendor. (3) No multi-tenancy primitives - per-tenant namespaces, quotas, isolation, per-tenant rate-limit accounting are mandatory for vendors serving hundreds-to-thousands of B2B customers (Persona, Socure, Castle, Fingerprint, Sumsub all bill per-tenant). (4) No triggers / 'fire webhook when geo_velocity > 1000 km/h' or 'fire when (visitor_id x asset_id).count crosses N in 24h' - identity vendors expose 'send a webhook when threshold crossed' to their own customers and re-implementing on top of polling 30-150 features per identify is wasteful. Cited as top-3 gap across all three relevant use cases. (5) No cross-region replication - a user logging in from EU then APAC within 30s would hit two different beava shards and the impossible-travel signal is lost across the partition (use case 19 documents this directly). Persona / Socure / Sumsub all run multi-region for data-residency. (6) Refuse-on-network-FS + in-memory-only means each region must plan local-NVMe WAL and bounded cold-start replay time; visitor_id / fingerprint blowup during a device-farm event could OOM the box, and a node restart at 50-200GB hot state cannot become an outage during an active attack. (7) No first-class HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K with documented memory budgets (may be present in the ~60-primitive count but not prominently documented) - visitor_id and (visitor_id x asset) cardinality require the Fingerprint 10k-cap-then-truncate pattern in bounded RAM. (8) No per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction at primitive granularity - GDPR Recital 47 + EDPB 2/2023 require differential retention (fraud-flagged identities retained longer, clean ones dropped sooner). (9) No GDPR / CCPA right-to-erasure tooling - bulk-delete by account_id / visitor_id, audit-logged. (10) No SOC-analyst surface ('show me all accounts with geo_velocity > 800 km/h in the last hour'); secondary indexes / top-K queries not available. (11) No Go / Rust / Java / Node client SDKs - IDV vendor platform teams live there, not Python. (12) No production benchmarks at 10^8+ keys with cardinality-driven memory and p99 latency curves - capacity-planning unproven for vendor-scale workloads. (13) No documented PII / hashing story (salted SHA-256 of IP / email / account_id_hash at rest, no raw email in state, per-primitive retention policy).
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo for the embedded-feature-backend motion (the realistic wedge); 12mo+ for vendor-replacement (not the right motion). To be sellable AS THE FEATURE BACKEND UNDERNEATH an identity-platform vendor or an in-house IDP team within 3-6 months, beava needs: TLS + token/mTLS auth (~1mo, addresses gap 1, blocks every regulated buyer today); threshold-crossing triggers / webhooks (~1-2mo, addresses gap 4, unlocks the most-cited gap across use cases 2, 19, 20); per-tenant namespaces + quotas + per-key TTL (~1-2mo, addresses gaps 3 + 8); HLL/CMS/Top-K first-class promotion in docs (~2-4 weeks if already present, addresses gap 7); GDPR right-to-erasure tooling (~2-4 weeks, addresses gap 9); Go + Rust client SDKs (~1-2mo, addresses gap 11); one flagship impossible-travel demo at python/beava/demos/impossible_travel (~1-3 days, addresses zero-traction validation gap and is the single highest-leverage marketing artefact beava can ship for the entire identity domain). In-process sharding and cross-region replication (gaps 2 + 5) are 6-12mo+ each and are not strictly required for the FIRST motion (single-binary regional / per-tenant deployment fits inside one box for any non-Fingerprint-scale buyer); they ARE required to displace a Redis Cluster / Aerospike deployment inside a Fingerprint-scale vendor.

Beava-specific traction in this segment: zero.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - lead with impossible-travel demo. Lead-eligible on technical fit (geo_velocity / distance_from_home / geo_spread are FIRST-CLASS in beava and not in any general-purpose competitor's primitive list - this is the single cleanest production-shaped operator advantage beava has across all 30+ use cases; the ~60-primitive catalogue is a near-exact shape match for what Fingerprint Velocity Signals, Sumsub Device Intelligence, Castle behavioural velocity, Sardine 4,800-feature store, and Socure Sigma Device productise), market urgency (Persona $200M / $2B May 2025 explicitly on agentic-AI thesis, ID.me $340M / $2B Sep 2025, Incode $3B target Nov 2025, Socure RiskOS + FedRAMP Mar 2025, Sumsub-Fingerprint Jun 2025, Castle-Cloudflare May 2025, World AgentKit + Prove + Google Cloud Fraud Defense + OpenAI/Stripe ACP in 2025-2026 - this segment is the most-funded fraud-adjacent thesis of the last 12 months), and Apache-2.0 wedge against both Redis post-relicense AND every proprietary product incumbent. Downgraded from Lead to Compete because (a) beava CANNOT replicate Persona/Socure/Incognia/Sumsub/Fingerprint identity-graph data moats and must explicitly position as feature-backend-underneath, not vendor-replacement; (b) hyperscaler bundling threat is Medium-not-Low (Entra ID Protection P2 ships impossible-travel as a default checkbox for any Azure-fronted enterprise; AWS Cognito advanced security covers basic risk-based auth); (c) zero beava-side traction and no packaged demo; (d) the realistic motion is 'feature backend embedded under a Persona / Socure / Castle / Fingerprint / Sumsub / in-house IDP equivalent', not 'beava replaces an IDV vendor'. PRIORITY ACTION: ship the impossible-travel demo at python/beava/demos/impossible_travel/ (1-3 day build on existing primitives) - this is the single highest-leverage marketing artefact beava can ship for the entire identity domain and the cleanest standalone flagship across the catalogue. SECONDARY ACTION: add TLS+auth + threshold-crossing triggers + Go/Rust client SDKs (~3-6mo) to unlock embedded-in-vendor pilots.
